output.name: Thorna

anatomy.part: butt end of the gaff shaft, at the bottom of the figure
the hand-grip, where the shaft bulges slightly
midshaft, where the pole bends back
the collar, where the shaft meets the hook
the crown of the hook, on its outer arc at the top
the barb tip, the outer point of the hook
the throat of the hook, on its inner edge where the barb curls back

output.myth: In high summer the big fish come up through the strait, the ones with teeth like bone combs, and they tear a net faster than a child can count the knots. My grandmother's mother said the first gaff was made by Ennu from a whalebone rib and a length of ash. Ennu gave it to Aun, who was never good at waiting. Aun leaned over the gunwale to see how deep the strait went, and Tavo came along laughing and filled the sail, and the fish came up all at once. Aun hooked one, and the gaff hooked him too, and the two of them hung there above the water while Tavo laughed himself hoarse. Kael cast his net for the fallen stars and caught nothing, as always, but he saw the gaff and kept quiet. Hesk counted the hauls and found one short. So when the big ones run, the gaff goes up over the strait, and we haul carefully, because Aun is still on the end of it.
output.verse:
Hang the gaff up high,
haul them quick, before they tear
the net. The last is Aun.

problems: The top hook is cramped. It reads as a small loop at the head of the shaft, not a clearly curled gaff hook, so the crown, barb and throat stars bunch together.
The labels for the crown of the hook and the barb tip overlap at the top right and are unreadable.
The collar label sits on the shaft just below the hook, but the collar star looks slightly low on the shaft rather than at the hook junction.
The hand-grip kink is subtle, so the bulge at the grip is hard to distinguish from the shaft line.
The blue outline runs as a stroke offset around the gold centre line, so it reads as a band rather than a true silhouette. That is acceptable, but the figure is thin and small in the frame.
The three background stars at the far left and top right are unrelated to the figure and could be mistaken for part of it.
judge.advice: The figure is the right way up: butt end (98761) at the bottom near (307,440), shaft rising to the hand-grip (98412) near (325,377), midshaft (98842) near (303,303) where it bends back, and the collar (98688) near (312,203) where the shaft meets the hook. Keep these. Improve the hook: widen it so the outer arc (98353, crown) rises above the collar, with the barb tip (98066) on the far right outer point and the throat (98162) on the inner edge where the barb curls back toward the shaft, around (330,168). Space these three stars further apart so their labels do not overlap, and move the crown and barb labels to opposite sides. Make the hand-grip bulge more pronounced so it reads as a grip. Verdict is keep: match and fit both clear the redraw threshold, but these refinements would raise the fit score.

guess: A shepherd's crook or walking cane, with a curled hook at the top and a long kinked shaft
